name: Die Cut Vinyl Stickers
seoTitle: Die Cut Vinyl Stickers in Bulk | The Die Cut Stickers
seoDescription: Die cut vinyl stickers cut to your artwork outline on white, clear or laminated vinyl, printed in bulk and wholesale runs. Free proof and free US shipping.
tagline: Printed vinyl cut to the shape of your logo, from 100 pieces to wholesale pallets.
quickAnswer: Die cut vinyl stickers are full-color stickers printed on white or clear vinyl and cut, backing included, to the outline of the artwork. They suit brands, merch sellers, event teams and resellers who want a logo or character with no square edge around it. Sizes run from 0.5 inches to 24 by 36 inches, pricing starts from $0.30 per sticker with a 100 piece minimum, and production takes 5 to 7 business days after proof approval.
highlights: Material: white or clear 3 mil vinyl

sections.h2: Shape-cut vinyl versus the standard vinyl sticker
sections.html:
Vinyl is the material; die cut is what we do with it. On this page the blade follows the outline of your artwork through the vinyl and the backing paper, so each sticker arrives as its own shape with the backing trimmed to match. Peel, press, done. Nothing white or clear hangs around the edge of the logo. The buyer who lands here usually has a mascot, a wordmark inside a badge, or an illustration with an irregular edge, and wants it in quantity.

The sibling page, custom vinyl stickers, is the general material page: squares, circles, rounded rectangles and kiss cut sheets, printed on the same film. Choose that when the artwork already fits a standard shape or when you want several designs on one sheet. Choose die cut when the shape is the point. If you are not sure which cut your artwork needs, the custom vinyl sticker page explains the kiss cut and sheet options in more detail.

sections.h2: Bulk runs: what changes at 1,000 and 5,000 pieces
sections.html:
Short runs print digitally, which is why 100 pieces of a one-off design is practical. Somewhere past a few thousand pieces of one artwork, offset becomes the better press: the plate cost spreads across the run and the unit price drops. We decide the press per job and you see one price either way. Wholesale buyers ordering die cut stickers in bulk usually fall into one of these groups:

  • Apparel and merch brands adding a sticker to every order as a packing insert
  • Trade show teams handing out 2 to 3 inch logo stickers across a season
  • Breweries, coffee roasters and taprooms selling stickers at the counter
  • Schools, teams and booster clubs reselling spirit stickers for fundraising
  • Resellers and promo companies who place white-label orders for their own clients
  • Software and gaming companies shipping sticker packs to a community

For resellers we pack by design and quantity with no branding on the box. The full catalog of cuts, materials and finishes we run alongside vinyl lives on our custom sticker homepage, which helps when a client asks for something outside this page.

sections.h2: Choosing the vinyl: white, clear or laminated
sections.html:
Four builds cover nearly every die cut vinyl order. The differences are in how the color reads and how long the sticker lasts outdoors.

Vinyl buildLookOutdoor lifeBest for
White gloss vinylBright, saturated color with shine2 to 3 years unlaminatedLogos, characters, merch packs
White matte vinylSoft, no glare, feels like paper2 to 3 years unlaminatedBrand marks on packaging, laptops
Clear vinylSurface shows through, white ink optional2 to 3 yearsBottles, glass, light surfaces
Laminated white vinylGloss or matte laminate over printTypically 3 to 5 yearsVehicles, coolers, outdoor gear

Lamination is the one upgrade worth paying for if the sticker will see sun, dishwashers or car washes. It adds a clear film over the ink so scratches and UV hit the film, not the print. Other films such as holographic, reflective and kraft are covered under our stickers by material listing.

sections.h2: Ordering a bulk die cut vinyl run step by step
sections.html:
1. Send the artwork as a vector file (AI, EPS, SVG, PDF) or a 300 dpi PNG with a transparent background. Transparent PNGs let us trace the cut line without guessing.
  2. Give the finished width in inches. Height follows the artwork proportion. Most logo stickers run 2 to 4 inches; bumper and cooler pieces run 5 to 8.
  3. Choose white or clear vinyl, gloss or matte, and whether to laminate.
  4. State the quantity per design. 100 is the minimum, and sizes of the same artwork can be combined to reach it.
  5. Approve the free digital proof. It shows the cut path and the backing shape; check thin tails and inner gaps here.
  6. Production runs 5 to 7 business days, then FedEx delivers free within the United States, 8 to 10 business days in total.

sections.h2: Keeping edges clean on complex shapes
sections.html:
A die cut is only as good as the path the blade follows. Give the artwork a bleed of 0.125 inches past the cut line so a slight registration shift does not leave a white sliver, or let us add a 0.0625 inch border in a color you choose, which hides the shift completely. Avoid spikes thinner than 0.1 inches and gaps narrower than that between parts of the design; the blade rounds them off and the vinyl between them tears on peel.

Wordmarks with separate letters need a shape behind them, a rounded rectangle or a simple outline, or every letter becomes its own tiny sticker. We flag this on the proof and suggest a fix rather than cutting what will not survive. Buyers with a sustainability brief sometimes ask for a non-vinyl option; our custom eco friendly sticker range uses recyclable paper and biodegradable film and can be die cut the same way.

faqs.q: Are die cut vinyl stickers cut through the backing too?
faqs.a: Yes. The blade goes through the vinyl and the backing paper, so each sticker arrives as its own shape rather than sitting on a square of liner. That is what separates die cut from kiss cut, where only the vinyl is cut and the backing stays whole as a sheet.

faqs.q: How does the price of die cut vinyl stickers change in bulk?
faqs.a: Pricing starts from $0.30 per sticker and falls as the quantity rises, because setup is spread over more pieces and large runs move from digital to offset printing. Size and lamination push the price up. Send the size and quantity for a quote; two or three quantity tiers on one request show the break points.

faqs.q: Do you print die cut vinyl stickers wholesale for resellers?
faqs.a: Yes. Resellers and promo companies order under their own name and we ship in plain boxes with no branding, packed by design and quantity. Many run a standing order of several designs each month. The minimum is 100 per design, and offset pricing kicks in on the larger wholesale runs.

faqs.q: Will die cut vinyl stickers peel on a water bottle that goes in the dishwasher?
faqs.a: A laminated vinyl sticker holds up to regular dishwasher cycles once it has cured for 24 hours on the bottle. Unlaminated vinyl survives hand washing but the ink dulls after repeated hot cycles. Apply to a clean, dry bottle and avoid wrapping across a seam where water can get under the edge.

faqs.q: How thick is the vinyl on a die cut vinyl sticker?
faqs.a: Our standard film is about 3 mil, with the laminate adding roughly another 1 to 2 mil. That is thick enough to peel without stretching and thin enough to lie flat over a gentle curve. Thicker 5 mil film is available for pieces that get handled a lot, such as equipment and toolbox stickers.

faqs.q: Can I split a 1,000 die cut vinyl sticker order between designs?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as each design reaches the 100 piece minimum. Ten designs at 100 each or two designs at 500 each both work. Each design gets its own proof and cut path. Pricing follows the quantity per design, so two designs at 500 cost more per piece than one design at 1,000.

faqs.q: Do die cut vinyl stickers fade in Arizona sun?
faqs.a: We print in Phoenix, so this gets tested daily. Unlaminated vinyl starts to soften in color after two or three summers of direct sun. Laminated vinyl typically holds three to five years. Stickers on a dashboard behind glass fade fastest because of the heat; a door or a cooler does far better.

faqs.q: What is the difference between die cut vinyl and kiss cut vinyl stickers?
faqs.a: Die cut goes through the vinyl and the backing, giving an individual shaped sticker. Kiss cut goes through the vinyl only, so the sticker peels off a larger backing sheet that can carry several designs. Die cut looks cleaner as a single piece; kiss cut is easier to peel and better for sticker sheets.

faqs.q: Can die cut vinyl stickers be made with a white border?
faqs.a: Yes. A border of about 0.0625 inches, white or any color, is the most common way to finish a die cut sticker. It hides tiny registration shifts between print and cut and gives a thin character to the edge. If you want the cut to run right to the ink, add a 0.125 inch bleed instead.

faqs.q: Which file works best for a die cut vinyl sticker shape?
faqs.a: A vector file, AI, EPS, SVG or PDF, with the cut line on its own layer if you have drawn one. If you only have a raster logo, a 300 dpi PNG with a transparent background is the next best, because the transparency gives us the outline to trace. Flattened JPGs on white need a manual trace.

faqs.q: How long does a bulk die cut vinyl sticker order take?
faqs.a: Production is 5 to 7 business days after you approve the free proof, and delivery by FedEx is free within the United States, so plan on 8 to 10 business days in total. Very large offset runs may need a day or two more for drying and cutting; we confirm that on the quote. Rush is available on request.

faqs.q: Can die cut vinyl stickers be removed from a laptop without residue?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Warm the sticker with a hair dryer for ten seconds, lift a corner with a fingernail and peel slowly at a low angle. Any tackiness left on the lid wipes off with isopropyl alcohol. If you expect to swap stickers often, ask for the removable adhesive when you order.
